record.original_question: Two metrics with negative curvature on a compact manifold must be isometric if they have the same marked length spectrum.

evidence.quote: Two metrics with negative curvature on a compact manifold must be isometric if they have the same marked length spectrum.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) smooth manifold, and let $g_1, g_2$ be two Riemannian metrics on $M$, each having strictly negative sectional curvature. For a metric $g$ of negative curvature on $M$, every free homotopy class $c$ of closed loops in $M$ contains a unique closed geodesic, whose $g$-length is denoted $\ell_g(c)$. The function $\ell_g : \mathcal{C}(M) \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, where $\mathcal{C}(M)$ is the set of free homotopy classes of closed loops in $M$, is called the marked length spectrum of $g$.

Prove or disprove: if $\ell_{g_1}(c) = \ell_{g_2}(c)$ for every free homotopy class $c \in \mathcal{C}(M)$, then there exists a diffeomorphism $\varphi : M \to M$ (isotopic to the identity) such that $\varphi^* g_2 = g_1$, i.e., $(M, g_1)$ and $(M, g_2)$ are isometric.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture (often attributed to Burns–Katok) is fully proven for closed surfaces of negative curvature by Otal (1990) and Croke (1990). In higher dimensions, the global conjecture remains open. Significant partial progress has been made: Hamenstädt obtained results under additional assumptions, and Guillarmou–Lefeuvre (Ann. of Math. 2019) proved local rigidity for Anosov manifolds (including all negatively curved closed manifolds), showing that two sufficiently close metrics with the same marked length spectrum are isometric. Subsequent work has extended this to quantitative and approximate rigidity statements, but the global problem in dimension ≥ 3 is still open.

status_evidence.title: The marked length spectrum of Anosov manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Guillarmou and Lefeuvre prove local rigidity of the marked length spectrum for Anosov Riemannian manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Local marked length spectrum rigidity is established for Anosov (in particular, negatively curved) closed manifolds, indicating the global problem is not yet resolved in higher dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Quantitative marked length spectrum rigidity for surfaces
status_evidence.snippet: For negatively curved surfaces, marked length spectrum rigidity was established by Otal and Croke.
status_evidence.claim: In dimension 2 the conjecture is solved (Otal, Croke).

status_evidence.title: Marked Length Spectrum Rigidity From Rigidity on Subsets
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to investigate marked length spectrum rigidity, indicating the higher-dimensional global conjecture is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The general higher-dimensional conjecture remains open as of 2025.
